description: Grade 5 example item: transpose an original concert-pitch melody to written pitch for clarinet in B flat, including respelling a chromatic note.

provenance.authoredBy: Music Theory Path curriculum team (Brief 01 example)

item.prompt: This melody is written at concert pitch. Transpose it UP a major 2nd, as it would be written for a clarinet in B♭. Use the correct new key signature.

music.textAlternative: Two bars in F major, 4/4, Andante. Bar 1: F, A, C, B natural (crotchets). Bar 2: C, D (crotchets), C (minim).

hints: First find the new key: a major 2nd above F major.
B♮ is a raised 4th degree in F major. What is the raised 4th degree in the new key?

feedback.correct: Correct. The new key is G major (one sharp), and the B♮ — a raised 4th in F — becomes C♯, the raised 4th in G. Remember to keep the tempo marking 'Andante'.

mistakes.wrong-direction: A B♭ clarinet sounds a tone lower than written, so its written part must be a tone HIGHER than concert pitch.
mistakes.key-signature-missing: Write the new key signature first: a major 2nd above F major is G major, with one sharp (F♯).
mistakes.accidental-not-adjusted: Don't copy the natural sign. B♮ is a raised 4th in F major; the raised 4th in G major is C♯.
mistakes.enharmonic-respelling: D♭ sounds the same as C♯, but each note must move up by a 2nd in letter names: B → C, so it is C♯.
mistakes.wrong-octave: Each note moves up by just a 2nd, so the melody stays in almost the same register.

feedback.fallback: Written for clarinet in B♭: G major — G, B, D, C♯ | D, E, D.
